unresolved_questions: What are the two receiver words at 0x114 and 0x124? No record for this target names a member at either displacement. The model reads 0x124 as a pointer because the body dereferences it, and 0x114 as a pointer for the same reason, and names neither.

What is the 12-byte frame buffer at [ESP+0x10] that 0x01053e67 forms and hands to the +0x30 slot? The body never reads it back -- it consumes the callee's EAX instead -- so whether it is a genuine second output or an artefact of the callee's prototype is not decidable from this body. The model passes it and does not look at it, and the model test proves the non-read by having the observer fill it with different words.

What are the three single-precision words copied at 0x01053e7f..0x01053ea2? MOVSS fixes that each is one 32-bit single-precision word at offsets 0, 4 and 8 of the pointer, and the model's type is named for that. Whether the three are a coordinate triple is not established by any record and is not claimed.

What are the six dispatched slots? The record's own unresolved_questions says their roles are inferred from shape only. The model gives each a name built from its displacement and asserts nothing else.

What is the table at 0x013f94d4? The bridge reads eight consecutive words there and all eight are code-range addresses. They are recorded in this sidecar as observed bytes; no value is asserted in the model and no record names the table.

Is the 0x01053e27 store before 0x01053e36 an ownership transfer or a bug? The store zeroes the receiver's word while ECX still holds the pointer, so the release-shaped transfer at 0x01053e36 is reached through a receiver that no longer names the object. That is what the listing does and the model reproduces it. Whether it is intended cannot be settled from this body, and the sibling at 0x01053db0 was not consulted for intent -- only for the frame shape.

What does 0x00cb5930 do with the second callee-popped stack word? Its own listing reads three consecutive words from it and writes them at offsets 0x13c, 0x140 and 0x144 of its receiver, and only after first trying to replace the pointer through its receiver's word at 0x134. Reading a three-word block out of a stack word that this body reloads from its own frame looks like an argument mix-up in the original; the model test treats 0x00cb5930 as an observer, so nothing is asserted either way, and whether the caller ever reaches that fallback is unknown (this body has fan_in 0).

Is the 0x01053e4d path -- a null word at 0x114 falling into a block that dereferences it with no test -- reachable in the original? The model reproduces the absence of the test and the model test does not enter that path. Whether any real caller can reach it needs a runtime observation, and this body has no recorded caller.

Which slot of the four associated tables does this entry occupy? It sits five words after the SDK-named func4Ch word in the tables based at 0x0149b810, 0x0149b900 and 0x0149ba30, but those regions interleave non-code words and the image has no RTTI, so the delta is reported and no slot number is claimed.

Why does the derived ABI record call the return register XMM0? abi_derived.return names XMM0 with register_class float_or_x87 and confidence APPROXIMATION, on the strength of the MOVSS instructions in the body. Both return paths set AL explicitly and no path writes XMM0 after 0x01053ea2, so the byte in AL is the return value. The record's XMM0 is reported and not adopted; the persisted record's AL and bool are what the model returns, and the RETURN SEMANTICS check compares the source against the persisted record.

The reconstruction declares a convention, and it is the machine's shape (two callee-popped dwords, RET 0x8), but the oracle is not proven, so the check says so. Note the record's persisted calling_convention is prose with no convention token in it, so there is no persisted claim for the source to contradict either -- a source declaring thiscall or stdcall does not FAIL this check, which is why the model declares stdcall.
expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS, and it is a real pass. The xref export carries exactly one outgoing direct-call row (0x01053ebf -> 0x00cb5930) and the complete 65-instruction listing carries exactly one direct transfer outside the body (the JMP at 0x01053e70 lands back inside and is excluded as intra-procedural). The source span names 0x00cb5930 by suffixing the VA onto the callee symbol, which is the convention _callee_addresses reads, and names no other. A reconstruction that named an extra callee, or omitted this one, would FAIL.

The listing names one data-segment address, 0x13f94d4 at 0x01053e57, and the source span names the same one, so the check takes the branch that reports an intersection without per-access read/write evidence. The converse -- a source that named no data address -- also WARNs here, on the branch that reports the listing's address with nothing to corroborate it against, because the xref export carries no data-reference edge type at all for this target (dependencies.data_reference_count is 0). There is no source-side choice that turns this into a PASS, and the honest resting state is the WARN.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: WARN, and this is the check that moves most between the two packages. The machine record names no receiver register and enumerates no offsets (see contradiction C1), so the grounded and absence arms are both unreachable: the model can declare displacements, but there is no receiver register to scan the listing under and no complete absence to attest. The arm reached is the one for a source that declares offsets with no machine-derived layout to corroborate them, and the span declares seven -- displacement 0x114, displacement 0x124, displacement 0x34, field table_00, field word_00, field word_04, field word_08. All seven are in the listing: the three displacements are the three the body addresses, and the four field names are the table pointer at displacement 0 of each object it dispatches through and the three single-precision words it copies. Declaring them is the honest choice: the listing shows all of them, and the alternative -- declaring none -- would score NOT_AVAILABLE, which is a worse verdict and a less accurate source. The WARN's own detail says no machine-derived struct layout exists to corroborate them, which is true and is the reason. The detail truncates its list to four names; the full seven were read out of the span directly.

The slot displacements are not among them because the model reaches them through named table members rather than literals, and that is deliberate -- it is what keeps the source span free of constants the listing's own receiver record cannot corroborate. Neither the record's five vtable associations nor the export's one vtable reference is read, because they are not independent of each other. survival_proof.M15: Genuinely indistinguishable, and proved rather than asserted. The three copies read three distinct members of a const-qualified object and write three distinct members of a local struct that nothing reads until all three stores have happened. A permutation of three independent load/store pairs over disjoint locations leaves the destination's contents bit-identical, and the destination's contents are the model's only observable output here -- the model test compares the triple handed to the +0x38 slot by value. There is no interleaving observer, no volatile and no aliasing, so no arrangement of the test can see the order. The reconstruction nonetheless keeps the listing's order (0x01053e7f, 0x01053e89 and 0x01053e94 map to word_00, word_04 and word_08) and the annotations name each instruction, because a mutation the test cannot see is still a mutation of the transcription. The limit is the test's, and it is recorded as one.
survival_proof.M16: A comment edit cannot be observed by any behavioural test. It is in the set to show the harness reports SURVIVED rather than passing everything, and it doubles as the control for the other sixteen.

mutation_check.detection_by_signal_note: M2, M4 and M9b are caught by SIGSEGV rather than by a named assertion, and that is stated rather than dressed up. All three are displacement or liveness errors that make the mutated model transfer control through a table word holding zero, or reach 0x01053ea8 with a cleared word at 0x124. The mutated model faults for the same reason the original would, and the assertion that would have named the fault is downstream of it. They are failures, not passes, and the distinction is recorded so a reader does not count 15 clean assertion failures.
